epithet: The small cheat, and the mighty Day
lede: A thumb on the scale: the most ordinary dishonesty there is. The surah begins there and sets it against the Day when all mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds — and shows that the man who shorts his customer is a man who has stopped believing in that Day.

names.name: al-Muṭaffifīn
names.note: After those it opens by condemning. Taṭfīf is to take a little — ṭafīf, a trifle — off what is owed: full measure when buying, less when selling. It is also called Sūrat al-Taṭfīf.

revelation.verdict: Differed over — at the threshold of the Hijrah
revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī gives three views. That it is Makkan is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Yaḥyā ibn Sallām. That it is Madinan is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah and Muqātil — with Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah excepting its last eight ayat as Makkan. The third, from Jābir ibn Zayd and al-Kalbī, is that it came down between the two cities, on the Hijrah itself. All three place it at the same moment: the traditional order makes it the eighty-sixth surah, the last before Madinah, and Muqātil called it the first revealed there.
revelation.when: At the very end of the Makkan years, or the first days in Madinah

evidence.quote: وَفِيها ثَلاثَةُ أقْوالٍ أحَدُها: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، والضَّحّاكُ، ويَحْيى بْنُ سَلامٍ. والثّانِي: مَدَنِيَّةٌ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، ومُقاتِلٌ
والثّالِثُ: أنَّها نَزَلَتْ بَيْنَ مَكَّةَ، والمَدِينَةِ، قالَهُ جابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ وابْنُ السّائِبِ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ المُطَفِّفِينَ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās and Ibn Mardawayh.

attested.quote: قالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ: وهي مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، والضَّحّاكِ، ومُقاتِلٍ، ومَدَنِيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةِ
attested.says: Citing al-Qurṭubī: Makkan in the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil; Madinan in the saying of al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrimah.

setting: Makkah was a city of merchants and Yathrib a city of farmers and markets, and in both of them trade was done with measures of volume and scales of weight that the seller held in his own hand. A man could keep two measures, one for buying and one for selling. Many did.

Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah its people were among the worst there were at measuring; then Allah sent down “Woe to those who give short measure”, and they measured well after that. Whether those opening ayat came down there, or had come down just before and were recited to them on his arrival, the report shows what the surah did: it changed how a town did business.

The surah’s argument runs from the stall to the Throne. Do such people not think they will be raised? The record of the wicked is kept; so is the record of the righteous. And it closes with a scene from the streets of Makkah — the powerful laughing at the believers, winking as they passed, going home pleased with themselves — and with that scene reversed.

occasions.title: The markets of Madinah
occasions.text: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah, they were among the worst of people in measuring. Then Allah sent down: “Woe to those who give short measure,” and they made good their measuring after that.
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā and Ibn Mājah (2223); ḥasan according to al-Albānī.

evidence.quote: عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: لَمَّا قَدِمَ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ ﷺ الْمَدِينَةَ كَانُوا مِنْ أَخْبَثِ النَّاسِ كَيْلًا فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾ فحسنَّوا الكيلَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ

aim: To set out the state of people in the scales and the stations of the next life — a threat to those who cheat and those who deny, and a comfort to the believers who are looked down on.

outline.title: Short measure
outline.summary: Woe to those who give short measure: who, when they take by measure from people, take in full, and when they measure or weigh for them, give less. Do they not think that they will be raised, for a tremendous Day — the Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?

outline.title: The record of the wicked
outline.summary: No — the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn: a register inscribed. Woe that Day to the deniers of the Recompense, each of them a sinful transgressor who, when Our ayat are recited to him, says, “Tales of the ancients.” No — what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts (83:14). That Day they will be veiled from their Lord; then they will enter the Blaze.

outline.title: The record of the righteous
outline.summary: No — the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn: a register inscribed, witnessed by those brought near. The righteous will be in bliss, on couches, looking on; you will know in their faces the radiance of delight. They are given a pure drink, sealed, its seal of musk — for that let those who compete, compete — mixed with Tasnīm, a spring from which those brought near will drink.

outline.title: Who laughs last
outline.summary: Those who did wrong used to laugh at those who believed, wink at one another as they passed, and go back to their people amused; and when they saw them they would say, “These are the ones astray.” But they were not sent as their keepers. So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers, on couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?

keyAyah.why: The Prophet ﷺ explained this ayah himself: each sin leaves a dark spot on the heart, and unrepented, they spread until they cover it.

virtues.text: “When the servant commits a sin, a black spot is marked on his heart. If he pulls away, asks forgiveness and repents, his heart is polished clean. If he returns, it is increased until it overspreads his heart. That is the rust that Allah has mentioned: ‘No — what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.’”
On “the Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds”, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Until one of them is sunk in his own sweat up to the middle of his ears.”

before: Al-Infiṭār spoke of noble scribes recording every deed. Al-Muṭaffifīn opens the two registers they write in.
after: Here the records are described where they are kept. Al-Inshiqāq shows them being handed over — to one in his right hand, to another behind his back.

notable.label: Woe to those who give short measure
The Day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds
For that let the competitors compete

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Sunan of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah
